rationale: Six patch findings in Build-image.ps1: Resolve-Path before Test-Path (validation order), missing daemon-liveness check, git stderr captured as branch/SHA on failure, fixed ctx/ path collides on concurrent invocations, nginx.conf copied without CRLF stripping, and ctx/ not removed after failed build. No spec artifact; acceptance lens not applicable; confidence is low. Zero findings deferred or dismissed.

findings.title: Resolve-Path runs before friendly directory guard
findings.problem: Resolve-Path is called at lines 15–17 before the Test-Path/throw guard at lines 25–27. A non-existent user-supplied root path triggers a cryptic PowerShell termination error from Resolve-Path, so the actionable 'Required directory not found' message is never reached.
findings.impact: A user passing a wrong BackendRoot, FrontendRoot, or PackagingRoot receives an opaque exception rather than the diagnostic the validation block was written to provide, making misconfiguration harder to diagnose.
findings.recommendation: Move the Resolve-Path calls to after the Test-Path validation loop at lines 25–27, or replace each Resolve-Path call with an inline Test-Path check and throw before calling Resolve-Path.

findings.title: No daemon-liveness check before context assembly
findings.problem: Lines 20–22 verify only that the engine binary exists on PATH. A stopped podman machine or non-running Docker Desktop is not detected; the script proceeds to assemble the full source context (steps 7–9) before failing at the build step with an opaque connection error.
findings.impact: Every invocation with a non-running daemon wastes time and performs unnecessary disk I/O copying backend, frontend, and packaging sources before the real error is surfaced.
findings.recommendation: After the binary check, add: '& $Engine info 2>&1 | Out-Null; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Engine ''$Engine'' daemon not reachable." }' to fail fast before context assembly.

findings.title: Git stderr captured as branch or SHA on rev-parse failure
findings.problem: Lines 78–79 use 2>&1 to redirect stderr into the capture but have no $LASTEXITCODE guard. If git fails (non-git directory, missing HEAD, etc.) the error text is stored in $branch or $sha and written to the build log as if it were a real ref.
findings.impact: The build log records false provenance — e.g. 'branch=fatal: not a git repository sha=fatal: not a git repository' — visually indistinguishable from a real branch name, undermining post-build traceability.
findings.recommendation: After each rev-parse call, check $LASTEXITCODE and substitute '(unknown)' on failure, matching the pattern already used for $dirtyLabel at line 81.

findings.title: Fixed ctx/ path collides on concurrent invocations
findings.problem: The context directory is always '$PSScriptRoot/ctx' (line 88). A second concurrent invocation from the same script location removes the first run's context at lines 89–95 mid-build.
findings.impact: Parallel CI jobs or overlapping developer retries from the same checkout produce non-deterministic build failures; reachability depends on usage patterns but the collision is confirmed possible on concurrent use.
findings.recommendation: Use a per-invocation path such as 'ctx-' + [System.Diagnostics.Process]::GetCurrentProcess().Id, or serialize invocations with a lock file before the Remove-Item.

findings.title: nginx.conf copied without CRLF stripping
findings.problem: Line 104 copies nginx.conf with Copy-Item, preserving any CRLF line endings from a Windows checkout (git autocrlf=true). The CRLF stripping applied to entrypoint.sh at lines 107–110 is not applied to nginx.conf.
findings.impact: On Windows with autocrlf enabled, nginx.conf enters the Linux container with \r\n endings; depending on the nginx version and directive, this may cause config parse errors and prevent the container from starting.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same ReadAllText/Replace/WriteAllText CRLF-stripping pattern used for entrypoint.sh to nginx.conf immediately after line 104.

findings.title: ctx/ not removed after failed build
findings.problem: Lines 165–169 run the engine build and exit with its exit code but do not remove $ctxDir on failure. The only cleanup is at the start of the next invocation (lines 89–95), so a failed run always leaves the full context tree on disk.
findings.impact: Repeated failed builds leave behind large ctx/ trees containing backend and frontend sources. On developer machines or CI agents running retries, this accumulates significant disk usage.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the build step in a try/finally block that removes $ctxDir when $buildExit is non-zero, or register a trap handler before the build invocation.
